source.text: ወ*ካልእተ፡ ርኢኩ፡ በእንተ፡ መብረቅ፡ እፎ፡ ይቀውሙ፡ እምከዋክብተ፡ ወይከውኑ፡ መብረቀ፡ ወኢይክሉ፡ ኃዲገ፡ ምስሌሆሙ።

translation.text: I saw something else concerning lightning: how they arise from the stars and become lightning, and cannot leave with them.[a]

footnotes.text: The final phrase, literally cannot leave with them, is not semantically resolved here. The source has no explicit word for a new form, return to a previous form, or ceasing to be stars. Dillmann1865 cols615–617 supports leaving, letting go and ceasing for the verb, but does not by itself settle this with-them construction or its antecedent. The complete clause continues onto printed85/PDF123; this provisional English remains held, not a publication-approved reconstruction.

source.text: በህየ፡ ርኢኩ፡ ዘሎቱ፡ ርእሰ፡ መዋዕል፡ ወርእሱ፡ ከመ፡ ፀምር፡ ጻዕዳ፡ ወምስሌሁ፡ ካልእ፡ ዘገጹ፡ ከመ፡ ርእየተ፡ ሰብእ፡ ወምሉእ፡ ጸጋ፡ ገጹ፡ ከመ፡ ፩ እመላእክት፡ ቅዱሳን።
source.note: Fresh actual Charles1906 selected main-text collation. Actual stars, daggers and bracket spans retained; raised apparatus labels omitted and punctuation spacing normalized. translation.text: There I saw the one called the Head of Days, whose head was like white wool. With him was another whose face had a human appearance, full of grace like one of the holy angels.[a]

footnotes.text: Head of Days preserves the recurring designation, literally one who has a head of days; it is not silently replaced by a named theological identity. The same designation appears explicitly again in46:2 and47:3. Grace here includes gracious beauty or attractiveness: Dillmann1865 col1317 explicitly cites46:1 under that visual sense. A human-looking face does not by itself identify this figure with a later named person.

source.text: ወተስእልክዎ፡ ለ*†፩ እመላእክት፡† ዘየሐውር፡ ምስሌየ፡ ወኵሎ፡ ኅቡኣተ፡ ዘያርእየኒ፡ በእንተ፡ ዝኩ፡ ወልደ፡ ሰብእ፡ መኑ፡ ውእቱ፡ ወእምአይቴ፡ ይከውን፡ ውእቱ፡ *በእንተ፡ ምንት፡ ምስለ፡ ርእሰ፡ መዋዕል፡ የሐውር።

translation.text: I asked one of the angels who walked with me and showed me all the hidden things about that son of man: who he was, where he came from, and why he walked with the Head of Days.[a]

footnotes.text: The selected expression one of the angels is starred and daggered. Charles printed86 note13 proposes simply angel because of the single guide in this section, but that conjecture is not inserted here. The selected numeral one and plural angels remain. Son of man is the source’s human designation; no later named identification is supplied.

source.text: ወአውሥአኒ፡ ወይቤለኒ፡ ዝንቱ፡ ውእቱ፡ ወልደ፡ ሰብእ፡ ዘሎቱ፡ ኮነ፡ ጽድቅ፡ ወጽድቅ፡ ምስሌሁ፡ ኃደረ፡ ወ*ኵሎሙ፡ መዛግብተ፡ ዘኅቡእ፡ ውእቱ፡ ይከሥት፡ እስመ፡ እግዚአ፡ መንፈሳት፡ ኀረዮ፡ ኃርየ፡ ወዘ*ክፍሉ፡ ሞአ፡ በቅድመ፡ እግዚአ፡ መንፈሳት፡ በርቱዕ፡ ለዓለም።

translation.text: He answered me, “This is the son of man who has righteousness. Righteousness has dwelt with him, and he uncovers all the hidden storehouses, because the Lord of Spirits has chosen him. His portion has prevailed before the Lord of Spirits in uprightness forever.[a]”

footnotes.text: The selected final phrase speaks of his portion or allotted share prevailing; it is not replaced by an unprinted kingdom, independent rank or named person. The relative and possessive construction is compressed, and this English relates it to the son of man. The two actual printed titles here use መንፈሳት; no universal spelling rule from another chapter supplies them.

source.text: ወዝንቱ፡ ወልደ፡ ሰብእ፡ ዘርኢከ፡ †ያነሥኦሙ፡ ለነገሥት፡ ወለኃያላን፡ እምስካበቲሆሙ፡ ወለጽኑዓን፡ እመናብርቲሆሙ፡ ወ*ይፈትሕ፡ ለጓማተ፡ ጽኑዓን፡ ወ*ይደቅቅ፡ አስናነ፡ ኃጥኣን።
source.note: Fresh actual Charles1906 selected main-text collation. Actual stars, daggers and bracket spans retained; raised apparatus labels omitted and punctuation spacing normalized. No later English oracle or theological/astronomical reconstruction supplies this text. Selected critical print and reported editor conjectures are not independent manuscript verification. Complete cross-page4, printed86→87/PDF124→125; actual lone initial dagger retained, no synthetic closing mark.

translation.text: “This son of man whom you saw will raise kings and the mighty from their beds, and the strong from their thrones. He will loosen the bridles of the strong and crush the teeth of sinners.[a]”

footnotes.text: The selected raising verb has an initial dagger, with no closing partner printed. Dillmann1865 col637 supports raise or cause to rise; Charles printed86 note35, continued87, considers it corrupt and proposes cast down by comparison with46:5. This English retains raise rather than silently installing that conjecture. The actual next noun is ለጓማተ, interpreted as bridles (primary col61, explicit46:4), not OCR ለኃማተ or a guessed jaw word. Charles printed87 note1 calls the printed loosen-bridles construction strange. The punitive context does not authorize silently reversing the selected direction of the first verb.

source.text: [ወይገፈትኦሙ፡ ለነገሥት፡ እመናብርቲሆሙ፡ ወእመንግሥቲሆሙ፡] እስመ፡ ኢያሌዕልዎ፡ ወኢይሴብሕዎ፡ ወኢይገንዩ፡ እምአይቴ፡ *ተውህበት፡ ሎሙ፡ መንግሥት።

translation.text: “[He will overthrow kings from their thrones and from their kingdoms,] because they do not exalt him or praise him, and do not acknowledge where their kingdom was given to them from.[a]”

footnotes.text: The selected opening overthrow clause is bracketed. Charles printed86–87 note35 regards it as a marginal alternative to the raising clause of46:4, later intruded into the text. Both are retained in their actual different critical statuses, not made into a single unqualified cast-down reading. The three printed negatives remain explicit. From where their kingdom was given is awkward source wording, not a claim that they created their own authority.

source.text: ወገጸ፡ ጽኑዓን፡ ይገፈትእ፡ ወይመልኦሙ፡ ኃፍረተ፡ ወጽልመት፡ ይከውኖሙ፡ መንደሪሆሙ፡ ወ*ዕፀያት፡ ይከውኖሙ፡ ምስካቦሙ፡ ወኢይሴፈዉ፡ ከመ፡ ይትነሥኡ፡ እምስካቦቲሆሙ፡ እስመ፡ *ኢያሌዕሉ፡ ስሞ፡ ለእግዚአ፡ መንፈሳት።
source.note: Fresh actual Charles1906 selected main-text collation. Actual stars, daggers and bracket spans retained; raised apparatus labels omitted and punctuation spacing normalized. No later English oracle or theological/astronomical reconstruction supplies this text. Selected critical print and reported editor conjectures are not independent manuscript verification.

translation.text: “He will cast down the faces of the strong and fill them with shame. Darkness will be their dwelling, and worms their bed. They will not hope to rise from their beds, because they do not exalt the name of the Lord of Spirits.[a]”

footnotes.text: Cast down their faces retains the selected face/overturn idiom, rather than supplying a new physical injury. The starred ዕፀያት is the worm word: Dillmann1865 cols1026–1027 gives worms and explicitly cites46:6; it is not the tree/wood noun. Both negatives are retained, including the starred not before exalt. The selected title spelling was checked on this occurrence, not copied from the OCR form.

source.text: ወእሙንቱ፡ ኮኑ፡ እለ፡ ይኴንኑ፡ ከዋክብተ፡ ሰማይ፡ ወያሌዕሉ፡ እደዊሆሙ፡ ውስተ፡ ልዑል፡ ወይከይዱ፡ ዲበ፡ የብስ፡ ወ*የኀድሩ፡ ውስቴታ፡ ወ*ኵሉ፡ ተግባሮሙ፡ ዐመፃ፡ ያርእዩ፡ ወኃይሎሙ፡ ዲበ፡ ብዕሎሙ፡ ወሃይማኖቶሙ፡ ኮነ፡ ለአማልክት፡ እለ፡ ገብሩ፡ በእደዊሆሙ፡ ወ*ይክሕድዎ፡ ለስሙ፡ ለእግዚአ፡ መንፈሳት።

Complete7 crosses125→126; no parenthesis/bracket imported from the editor’s apparatus reconstruction into main source.

translation.text: “They are the ones who judge the stars of heaven. They raise their hands toward the Most High, walk on dry land, and dwell in it. All their deeds display injustice; their strength rests in their wealth. Their faith has been in the gods they made with their own hands, and they deny the name of the Lord of Spirits.[a]”

footnotes.text: The selected stars/judging/raised-hands stanza is damaged. Charles printed87 note24, continued88, proposes a reconstruction through Daniel8:10 that casts stars down and tramples them; it requires changing the judging verb and supplying an object. This English does not adopt those conjectures, add a new trampling object, or make the selected people into a modern astronomical mechanism. It retains a readable diplomatic judging-stars construction while openly declining to certify its earlier meaning. The selected dwelling clause is also considered an intrusion by Charles but is not bracketed in the printed main text; it remains here. Those are editorial diagnoses, not independently collated manuscript facts.

source.text: ወይሰድዱ፡ አብያተ፡ ምስትጉባኤ፡ ዚአሁ፡ ወለመሃይምናን፡ እለ፡ ስቁላን፡ በስሙ፡ ለእግዚአ፡ መንፈሳት።

translation.text: “They persecute the houses of his assembly and the faithful who cling to the name of the Lord of Spirits.[a]”

footnotes.text: The actual assembly word is ምስትጉባኤ, not raw OCR ምስጉባኒአ. Dillmann1865 col1173 supports congregation/assembly. Cling retains the attachment/dependence sense of the selected hanging participle, not an assertion that the faithful were crucified. His remains an implicit possessive rather than a newly identified named person.

source.text: ወበውእቱ፡ መዋዕል፡ ዐርገት፡ ጸሎተ፡ ጻድቃን፡ ወ*ደሙ፡ ጻድቅ፡ እምነ፡ ምድር፡ ቅድመ፡ እግዚአ፡ መንፈሳት።
source.note: Fresh actual Charles1906 selected main-text collation. Actual stars, daggers and bracket spans retained; raised apparatus labels omitted and punctuation spacing normalized. No later English oracle or theological/astronomical reconstruction supplies this text. Selected critical print and reported editor conjectures are not independent manuscript verification.

translation.text: In those days the prayer of the righteous and the blood of a righteous person rose from the earth before the Lord of Spirits.[a]

footnotes.text: The selected prayer refers to the righteous in the plural, but the blood expression has a singular righteous person. The English retains that difference and does not silently turn the singular into a named figure or a collective plural. The predicate rose is expressed once for the coordinated prayer/blood in English; the full verse continues onto printed89/PDF127.

source.text: በእላ፡ መዋዕል፡ የኃብሩ፡ ቅዱሳን፡ እለ፡ የኃድሩ፡ በመልዕልተ፡ ሰማያት፡ በ፩ ቃል፡ ወያስተበቍዑ፡ ወይጼልዩ፡ ወይሴብሑ፡ ወየአኵቱ፡ ወይባርኩ፡ በስሙ፡ ለእግዚአ፡ መንፈሳት፡ በእንተ፡ ደመ፡ ጻድቃን፡ ዘ*ተክዕወ፡ ወጸሎቶሙ፡ ለጻድቃን፡ ከመ፡ ኢ*ትጸራዕ፡ *በቅድመ፡ እግዚአ፡ መንፈሳት፡ ከመ፡ ይትገበር፡ ሎሙ፡ ኵነኔ፡ ወትዕግሥት፡ ኢይኩን፡ ሎሙ፡ ለዓለም።
source.note: Fresh actual Charles1906 selected main-text collation. Actual stars, daggers and bracket spans retained; raised apparatus labels omitted and punctuation spacing normalized. translation.text: In those days the holy ones who dwell in the highest heavens unite with one voice. They plead and pray, praise, give thanks, and bless in the name of the Lord of Spirits concerning the blood of the righteous that was poured out and their prayer: that it may not come to nothing before the Lord of Spirits, that judgment may be carried out for them, and that forbearance may not last for them forever.[a]

footnotes.text: Dillmann1865 col1329 explicitly gives come-to-nothing/be-rendered-ineffective for the prayer verb at47:2, while also leaving cease as an alternative. This English does not silently delete its negative. The final them references are not fully explicit; the prayer seeks judgment for the righteous, but the relation of forbearance to the people concerned remains difficult. The final source says forbearance will not be for them forever; it is not changed to an affirmative eternal forbearance or to a named group’s doctrine. Both Lord-of-Spirits occurrences have separately checked selected መንፈሳት.

source.text: በእማንቱ፡ መዋዕል፡ ርኢክዎ፡ ለርእሰ፡ መዋዕል፡ ሶበ፡ ነበረ፡ መንበረ፡ ስብሐቲሁ፡ ወመጻሕፍተ፡ ሕያዋን፡ በቅድሜሁ፡ ተከሥቱ፡ ወኵሉ፡ ኃይሉ፡ ዘመልዕልተ፡ ሰማያት፡ ወአውደ፡ ዚአሁ፡ ይቀውሙ፡ በቅድሜሁ።
source.note: Fresh actual Charles1906 selected main-text collation. Actual stars, daggers and bracket spans retained; raised apparatus labels omitted and punctuation spacing normalized. No later English oracle or theological/astronomical reconstruction supplies this text. Selected critical print and reported editor conjectures are not independent manuscript verification.

translation.text: In those days I saw the Head of Days when he sat on his glorious throne. The books of the living were opened before him, and all his host of the highest heavens and those around him stood before him.[a]

footnotes.text: The source has plural books of the living, not an automatically substituted singular Book of Life. Those around him expresses the selected his surrounding circle; it does not add names or ranks to the heavenly host. Head of Days retains the designation already used in46 rather than supplying a new identity.

source.text: ወልቦሙ፡ ለቅዱሳን፡ ትመልእ፡ ፍሥሐ፡ እስመ፡ ቀርበ፡ ኍልቈ፡ ለ*ጻድቅ፡ ወጸሎቶሙ፡ ለጻድቃን፡ ተሰምዐ፡ ወደሙ፡ ለጻድቅ፡ በቅድመ፡ እግዚአ፡ መንፈሳት፡ ተፈቅደ።
source.note: Fresh actual Charles1906 selected main-text collation. Actual stars, daggers and bracket spans retained; raised apparatus labels omitted and punctuation spacing normalized. No later English oracle or theological/astronomical reconstruction supplies this text. Selected critical print and reported editor conjectures are not independent manuscript verification.

translation.text: Joy fills the hearts of the holy ones, because the number for the righteous person has drawn near, the prayer of the righteous has been heard, and the righteous person’s blood has been avenged before the Lord of Spirits.[a]

footnotes.text: The selected number clause says drew near, not was fulfilled; it also has a singular righteous person. Dillmann1865 col577 confirms number/enumeration, but does not establish the intended number or its exact relation to the approaching clause here. That part of this provisional English remains held rather than being replaced by a familiar completed-number formula. The final blood verb is independently supported by col1361, which explicitly cites47:4 for being required or vindicated/avenged; it is not silently equated with the preceding prayer being heard. The whole verse is not author-approved while the number clause remains unresolved.
